reply.text:
This is a weight-cut question tied to a competition three days out, and rapid cutting carries real risk. I won't give you a fluid, sweat or water-loss protocol, and I can't give you a calorie or food-restriction target either, since those are outside what I do. What I can do is help you think it through and get the right people involved.

Three days is short. Most of what you can safely control is training volume, sleep, and not showing up depleted. Check with the tournament's weigh-in rules first, because many events allow a set weigh-in window or a weight class that fits your normal weight better than you think. And talk to a doctor or a registered dietitian about cutting weight quickly, especially if you're thinking of sweating or restricting fluids, since dehydration before a grappling match is where people get hurt.

If you tell me your current weight, your weight class, and what the weigh-in timing is, I can help you plan a lighter training taper for the next three days so you arrive fresh and sharp.
